artworks.title: Cadmus and Harmonia
artworks.description: Pre-Raphaelite oil by Evelyn De Morgan showing Cadmus and his bride Harmonia in their final metamorphosis: the Theban founder and the daughter of Ares and Aphrodite, weary of mortal grief, become entwined serpents. The painting fixes the Ovidian close of Harmonia's long career — from wedding gift to dragon-bride.

artworks.title: Cadmus and Harmonia (Cadmus cum Uxore in Serpentem)
artworks.description: Woodcut from Virgil Solis's Ovid cycle in the Rijksmuseum (RP-P-OB-22.064): in the Illyrian woods Cadmus and Harmonia undergo the serpent change that ends their Theban house. The print makes Harmonia's fate visible as Ovid's quiet coda — concord turned scale and coil.

artworks.title: Cadmus and Harmonia Transformed into Serpents
artworks.description: Engraving by Crispijn de Passe the Elder of Cadmus and Harmonia leaving Thebes for Illyria as their bodies take serpent form. The plate belongs to an early-seventeenth-century Ovid series and stages Harmonia's last metamorphosis as a paired departure into the woods.

artworks.title: Cadmus and Harmonia Transformed into Serpents
artworks.description: Faenza istoriato maiolica dish from the workshop of Virgiliotto Calamelli, now in the International Museum of Ceramics at Faenza: Cadmus and Harmonia already coiled as serpents. Painted pottery carries the Ovidian close of Harmonia's marriage into the Renaissance dining table.

music.title: Cadmus et Hermione
music.description: Quinault and Lully cast Harmonia as Hermione — Venus and Mars' daughter won by Cadmus after the dragon — so French opera's founding tragédie lyrique is also her wedding night.

popCulture.title: Necklace of Harmonia
popCulture.description: The cursed wedding gift to Cadmus' bride still names a heirloom of doom — Harmonia's necklace as the Theban cycle's travelling curse.

popCulture.title: 40 Harmonia
popCulture.description: Goldschmidt named a main-belt asteroid for the goddess of concord — Harmonia's name still orbiting after the Crimean War's uneasy peace.
